## Hypothesis

H1: The perceived morality of infidelity (IV) will effect willingness to marry without love (DV).

H2: Sex (categorical IV) will affect time spent dressing well (DV).

```{r load package}
library(codebook)
raw <- read.csv("/Users/srb/R Studio/PSY 221A/PSY221A-HW/lab02_files/data_doctored.csv")
```

## Load the processed data

```{r loadData}
#load processed data
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)
install.packages("ggrain")

h1Data <- read.csv("/Users/srb/R Studio/PSY 221A/PSY221A-HW/data/processed_data/h1.csv")
h2Data <- read.csv("/Users/srb/R Studio/PSY 221A//PSY221A-HW/data/processed_data/h2.csv")
#reorganize categorical variable
table(h2Data$Sex_birth)
h2Data$Sex_birth <- factor(h2Data$Sex_birth,
                           levels = c("Male","Female","Intersex"))

```

## H2 - Box Plot

```{r H2Box}
#Box plot
#The line is the median; the box covers the middle 50% of responses (Q1-Q3).
#Whiskers reach the most extreme observations within 1.5 IQR of the box edges.
h2Box <- ggplot(data=h2Data,
                aes(x=Sex_birth,
                    y=Time_A_dress_1,
                    fill=Sex_birth))+
  geom_boxplot () +
  labs(x="Sex assigned at birth",
        y="Amount of time spent on dressing well",
        title="Time spent dressing well by sex")+
  theme_gray(base_size=8) #changes font size

h2Box
```

## H1 - Violin Plot (with Box Plot)

```{r H1Violin}
#Violin Plot
#Wider sections show where responses are more concentrated within each group.
#The shape depends on smoothing; integer scores can create bumps.
h1Viol <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                aes(x=Sex_birth,
                    y=preference_imp_physat,
                    fill=Sex_birth))+
  labs(x="Sex assigned at birth",
        y="Points allocated to partner physical attractiveness",
        title="Points allocated to physical attractiveness by sex")+
  theme_gray(base_size=8)+
  geom_violin()+ #order doesn't usually matter
  geom_boxplot(width=.12)


h1Viol
```

## H1 - Raincloud Plot

```{r H1Raincloud}
#Raincloud Plot
#A raincloud combines a half-violin, a box plot, and individual responses.
h1Rain <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                aes(x=Sex_birth,
                    y=preference_imp_physat,
                    fill=Sex_birth))+
  labs(x="Sex assigned at birth",
        y="Points allocated to partner physical attractiveness",
        title="Points allocated to physical attractiveness by sex",
       fill="")+
  geom_rain(alpha=.5)+
  theme(minimal(base_size))

h1Rain
```

## H2 - Scatter Plots

```{r H2Scatter}
#Scatter Plot; commitment is the composite variable
h2Point <- ggplot(data=h2Data,
                  aes(x=qoa,
                      y=commitment))+
  geom_point()+
  labs(x="Confidence finding alternatives",
       y="Commitment level",
       title="Relationship between confidence finding alternatives and commitment level")+
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8)

h2Point

#Plot looks weird... why?
# They're on top of each other, and because of the composite variable and because qoa is only integers
nrow(h2Data) #There's fifty thousand data points, but the graph wasn't showing it
nrow(unique(h2Data[,c("qoa","commitment")]))

#Jitter
h2Jitter <- ggplot(data=h2Data,
                  aes(x=qoa,
                      y=commitment))+
  geom_jitter(width=.12,height=.04,alpha=.04,size=.6)+
    labs(x="Confidence finding alternatives",
       y="Commitment level",
       title="Relationship between confidence finding alternatives and commitment level")+
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8)

h2Jitter # know where data points are concentrated

```

## H2 - Smooth Line

```{r}
#Scatter Plot with line
h2Line <- h2Jitter + geom_smooth(method= "lm")
h2Line
  
```

## Save figures

```{r saveFigures}
#Run after creating the plots. Save PNG files in the project's figures folder.
dir.create("practiceFigures")
ggsave("practiceFigures/H1_figures_rainCloud.png", plot = h1Rain, width=10, height=6, dpi=300)
ggsave("practiceFigures/H2_digures_line.png", plot = h2Line, width=10, height=6, dpi=300)
```
